item.description: ...[skip-tooth] An old design of bicycle chain that was commonly used in the early 20th century. Unlike modern chains, where every link has a tooth, skip tooth chains have a tooth on every other link. A "skip tooth chain," also known as a "block chain," is an older design of bicycle chain that was commonly used in the early 20th century. item.description: ...chain wear < Bicycles | Maintenance and Repair | Chains This chain is not worn out yet A worn out chain Chains increase in length over time due to wear on the pins and bushings. Continuing to use a chain that is beyond a reasonable length can not only cause the chain to "skip" when pedalling under pressure but will also wear out the rest of your drivetrain as the teeth on the cassette/freewheel and chainrings try to match the length of the chain.
